text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should add a visible server-side skip link at the top of every page, allowing all users to bypass navigation. This decision prioritizes inclusivity for screen reader and keyboard users, who may struggle with repetitive navigation. By doing this, we're accepting the potential trade-off of added visual clutter for sighted users, but it's a worthwhile sacrifice for making the site usable for everyone. This approach also aligns with our quality-first principle, ensuring a solid foundation for accessibility.

name: Reader
text: I'm flagging the server-side skip link idea because it forces every user to download and parse an extra element, which may not be necessary for most users. A better alternative is to implement a client-side solution, but with a fallback for JavaScript-disabled or slow-loading scenarios. To settle this, I need to see data on how many users rely on screen readers or keyboard navigation versus those who would be slowed down by the extra element, and consider a solution that balances these competing needs.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a client-side skip link that appears only when keyboard focus reaches the first interactive element. This keeps the page clean for mouse users while giving keyboard and screen reader users instant access to main content. The trade-off is a tiny JavaScript payload that runs only on focus, not a full server-side element every page loads.

name: Reader
text: The client-side skip link that activates only on keyboard focus could create confusion for users who rely on screen readers, as it may not provide a visible cue for when the skip link is available. A better alternative is to ensure that the skip link is always visible, regardless of focus, which provides a more consistent experience. To settle this argument, let's conduct user testing with both options to gather feedback on usability and accessibility for different user groups.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a hybrid skip link—always visible but hidden off-screen until focused, with a fallback to server-side if JS fails. Result: EXCAVA meets WCAG 2.2 Level A for keyboard navigation. Owner: accessibility-w1.
